turns.t: Hi Mr Lowe, I'm Hannah, the nurse. Can I do your blood pressure and pulse while we wait for the doctor? ~
Yes, of course. Is that okay? I'm always nervous in here, my pressure goes through the roof. ~
Blood pressure 142 over 90, pulse 88. That's a touch up, but you're allowed to be nervous.
Hello, Mr Lowe. It's about six weeks since you started the physio and the heel pads. How are the heels?
A bit better, I think, but not right. I still get this pain at the back of both heels, especially first thing in the morning.
How long does the morning pain last?
Half an hour, maybe an hour. And then it eases once I'm up and moving. I'm worried it's something nasty.
Do you get back stiffness as well, in the morning?
No, my back's fine. No stiffness at all.
What are you taking at the moment?
Naproxen, 500 mg, twice a day, with food. It helps a bit.
Remind me of your other conditions.
Psoriasis, on my elbows, since my twenties. I had a red, sore eye once, iritis I think they said, two years ago. And acid reflux.
That history is useful, because those conditions can be linked. Let me see your heels. Can you lie on the couch? ~
Yes, sorry, my feet are a bit cold. ~
I'll put a blanket over you.
Tender at the back of both heels, right where the Achilles tendon attaches to the bone, and there's no swelling or redness of the tendons.
Is it a tear? I read about Achilles tears. ~
No, a tear would feel different, with a sudden pain and weakness. This is irritation where the tendon meets the bone. ~
So what's causing it? ~
Psoriasis, a past inflamed eye, and morning heel pain at the tendon attachments make me think I can't rule out an inflammatory arthritis linked to psoriasis.
Arthritis? At forty-four? ~
It can happen at any age, and it's treatable. I don't want to jump to conclusions, which is why we'll look more carefully. ~
Will it get worse? ~
If it is inflammatory, treating it early protects the joints. That's the reason to find out. ~
Doctor, shall I book him with the rheumatologist? ~
Yes please, Hannah. I'd like you to see a specialist, Mr Lowe, and I'd like to see you in six weeks as well.
Six weeks. Right. ~
Keep up with the stretches and the heel pads, and avoid hard flat shoes.
I will. Thank you, doctor. You've calmed me down. ~
See you in six weeks, Mr Lowe. ~
